analysis.title: GS Basics - Brazil Surprise. Cost of Capital. Nets Down.
key_insights: Feared weekend escalation against Iran did not materialize. Diplomatic discussions continue and talks are ongoing today, though the author calls the hope slim.
French protests were more contained than previous episodes, so a downgrade was avoided.

Lula overturned a first-round deficit to win the Brazilian election, with legal challenges looming. The result was far from prediction market expectations, so the author expects sizable pressure across Brazilian assets and second-order exposures.
US equities were sold for a third consecutive week, with the largest single-stock de-grossing since July. TMT saw about $20bn sold over two weeks.

Fundamental nets are at YTD lows but gross exposure is still at the 63rd percentile. Global tech selling is -3.3 sigma over two weeks, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4:1. Single stocks have been sold for six consecutive weeks.
Performance is poor across discretionary L/S, multi-strats and quants. The author says gross, not nets, is what hurt last week.

Hyperscaler and data center credit spreads have widened across the capital structure, compounded by execution and refinancing risks. The author says the cost of capital has repriced and there is no obvious solution, while demand optimism remains.

Hyperscaler capex outcomes: worst case is capex accelerating funded by expensive debt, arguably worse is capex cut because financing is unavailable, best case is capex rising with accelerating organic cash flow and a path to self-funding through 2027/28, and the middle ground is flat/up capex with more equity financing (bad for hyperscaler equity, potentially good for credit).
Google, Microsoft and Amazon results are critical this week. The focus is on how backlog converts to cloud revenue and how the next leg of capex is financed.
Busy macro week: UK Budget with potential bank taxes (growing client interest in shorting the UK domestic consumer basket), China policy meetings, US 2yr/5yr/7yr supply, ECB, BOJ and FOMC.

The market expects the Fed to skip. The question is whether Warsh focuses on recent hot inflation or acknowledges how aggressively financial conditions have tightened. AI and nominal-growth investors hope for the latter.

Most clients are playing defense and conviction is hard to find. Positioning, sentiment and performance are severely constrained, with shorts squeezing and nothing working. The author says it would not take much to stabilize risk but there is no catalyst, and hyperscaler guidance and the Fed are the obvious candidates with two-sided risks.

Energy remains critical. The author is confused by a policy that telegraphed escalation and let markets pre-price an energy shock, and suggests it may be maximum military pressure ahead of a last-minute grand bargain.

sector_views.rationale: Demand outlook is positive, but the repricing of the cost of capital and financing risk around capex weigh on hyperscaler equity. The middle-ground outcome is bad for hyperscaler equity and potentially good for credit.
Growing client interest in shorting the UK domestic consumer basket ahead of potential bank taxes in the UK Budget.

earnings_insights: Google, Microsoft and Amazon earnings this week are described as critical. The focus is on capex intentions, backlog conversion into cloud revenue and how the next leg of capex is financed. No estimates are given.

macro_indicators.reading: Market expects the Fed to skip
macro_indicators.interpretation: Focus is on whether Warsh stresses recent hot inflation or the tightening of financial conditions. The latter would help AI and nominal-growth exposures.
Small caps outperformed while tech sold off.
Broad equal-weight strength against a weak Nasdaq.
Semis sold sharply, and Asia semis are catching down to the US close.

tension_points.bear_case: Capex accelerates funded by expensive debt, or is cut because financing is unavailable. Credit spreads across the capital structure have already widened.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Google, Microsoft and Amazon guidance this week on how backlog converts to cloud revenue and how the next leg of capex is financed.
